Tips and traps

  • Remember
    Write the loop as a generator with yield from. The caller sees one long stream of items and can stop early, and pages are only fetched when they are needed.Lesson: Pagination: getting every page
  • In the exam
    A token bucket holds up to capacity tokens and refills rate tokens every second. Each call takes one token, and with no token the call must wait or gets 429. So it allows short bursts but keeps the average at the rate. Servers use it to protect themselves, and clients can use it to stay polite.Lesson: Rate limits: the token bucket
  • Remember
    By default pydantic ignores fields it does not know (like "extra" above). Set model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid") to reject them, or strict=True to refuse "7" for an int.Lesson: Checking the data with pydantic

Step 3Web and APIs · Flask: small and flexible web apps

3.1

Flask basics: routes, templates, forms and JSON

Open chapter

Flask routes, request and response, Jinja templates, forms and sessions, a JSON API and running the app.

Key ideas

  • Routes @app.route(rule, methods=[...]) or @app.get / post. Converters string, int, float, path, uuid. url_for(endpoint, **values). 404 no match, 405 wrong method.
  • Request request.args.get(name, default, type=int), request.form, request.get_json(silent=True), request.files, headers, cookies.
  • Responses str is HTML, dict or list is JSON, (body, status, headers), redirect(url_for(...)), abort(code), make_response, @app.errorhandler(404).
  • Templates and sessions render_template, {{ }} escaped, {% for %}, filters, extends and block. session is a signed cookie, needs secret_key. flash and get_flashed_messages.
  • Run and test app.test_client() for tests. flask --app app run --debug only on your computer. gunicorn -w 4 "app:app" in production.

Formulas

Requests in progress (Little's law)Exam favourite
L = λ × W
120 requests/s, 0.2 s each: 24 requests at the same moment, so at least 24 workers or threads.
Lesson: The maths: workers, time and limits
Gunicorn starting point
workers = 2 × CPU cores + 1
4 cores: 9 worker processes.
Lesson: The maths: workers, time and limits
Throughput of sync workersExam favourite
requests/s ≤ workers / time per request
9 workers, 50 ms each: 9 / 0.05 = 180 requests/s.
Lesson: The maths: workers, time and limits
Python time limit with threads (GIL)
requests/s ≤ 1 / CPU time per request, per process
10 ms of Python per request: at most 100 requests/s for one process, however many threads.
Lesson: The maths: workers, time and limits
Cookie size
base64 makes data 4 / 3 as big
A 4,096 byte cookie holds about 3,072 bytes of session data.
Lesson: The maths: workers, time and limits
Error rate
rate = errors / requests × 100 %
30 errors out of 600 requests: 5 %.
Lesson: The maths: workers, time and limits

No.ProblemLevelPatternHint
434Number of Segments in a StringEasystr.split() with no argumentLike counting the words a user typed into a search box. split() with no argument skips any amount of spaces, so empty parts never appear.
1662Check If Two String Arrays are EquivalentEasyJoin and compareA page built from template parts must give the same text however it was cut. Join both lists and compare the results.
1544Make The String GreatEasyA stack of lettersCleaning user input with a stack. Push each letter, but pop instead when it is the same letter in the other case as the top.
2696Minimum String Length After Removing SubstringsEasyA stack removes pairs as they appearRemoving "AB" and "CD" again and again is the same as a stack that pops when the new letter completes a pair with the top.
648Replace WordsMediumCheck the shortest roots firstLike a router that finds the shortest registered prefix of a path. Put the roots in a set and try prefixes from short to long.
1209Remove All Adjacent Duplicates in String IIMediumA stack of [letter, count]Keep each letter with how many times it repeats on top of the stack. When the count reaches k, pop the whole group.
820Short Encoding of WordsMediumDrop words that are endings of other wordsA word that is the end of another word needs no space of its own. Remove every ending of every word from a set, then add len(word) + 1 for each word that is left.
916Word SubsetsMediumMerge the needs into one CounterA word is universal when it has every letter of every word in words2, as often as needed. Merge words2 into one Counter of the largest counts, then check each word once.
30Substring with Concatenation of All WordsHardCut each window into words and compare CountersFind every place where all the words appear joined in any order, like spotting a set of template parts in a page. Each window has a fixed length, so cut it into word sized pieces and compare counts.
224Basic CalculatorHardA stack of (result, sign) for each bracketTemplates and config files evaluate small expressions. Walk the text, build numbers digit by digit, and push the result so far when a bracket opens.
Lesson: LeetCode practice

Tips and traps

  • Remember
    Build links with url_for("hello", name="Bob") and never by hand. If you rename a URL later, every link still works, and url_for escapes special characters for you. Extra arguments become the query string, as with page=3 above.Lesson: Routes and URLs
  • In the exam
    A route answers only GET (and HEAD, OPTIONS) unless you pass methods=. A wrong method gives 405 Method Not Allowed, a URL that matches no rule gives 404 Not Found.Lesson: Routes and URLs
  • Remember
    request looks like a global variable, but each request in each thread sees its own. Flask does this with context variables, so two users at the same moment never see each other's data.Lesson: The request and the response
  • Common mistake
    Jinja escapes every value by default in .html templates, so a name such as <script> is shown as text and never runs. This stops cross site scripting (XSS). Only mark text as safe with |safe when you made it yourself.Lesson: Templates with Jinja
  • Common mistake
    The session cookie is signed, NOT encrypted: the example decodes it and reads the user name. Never put secrets in it, keep secret_key secret and long, and read it from an environment variable.Lesson: Forms, sessions and flash messages
  • In the exam
    Real forms also need protection against cross site request forgery (CSRF), so another website cannot post forms as your user. The extension Flask-WTF adds a hidden token to every form and checks it.Lesson: Forms, sessions and flash messages
  • Remember
    @app.get, @app.post, @app.put, @app.patch and @app.delete are short forms of @app.route with one method. They make an API easier to read.Lesson: A JSON API in Flask
  • Common mistake
    A global dict like BOOKS is fine for learning, but it is lost when the server restarts, and each Gunicorn worker process has its own copy. Real apps keep data in a database, as the next chapter shows.Lesson: A JSON API in Flask
3.2

Real Flask apps: structure, database, login and tests

Open chapter

Application factory, blueprints, sqlite3, login with hashed passwords, pytest, config and deployment.

Key ideas

  • Structure create_app(settings) returns a new app. Blueprint(name, __name__, url_prefix=...), app.register_blueprint(bp). url_for("bp.view"). current_app, not a global app.
  • Database get_db() on g, sqlite3.Row, ? placeholders, commit(), app.teardown_appcontext(close_db), @app.cli.command("init-db").
  • Auth generate_password_hash / check_password_hash (salted, slow). session.clear() then session["user_id"]. before_app_request loads g.user. login_required with functools.wraps.
  • Tests pytest fixture in conftest.py builds create_app({"TESTING": True}) and returns app.test_client(). app.test_cli_runner() for commands.
  • Production Config from environment (from_prefixed_env), app.logger, errorhandler passing HTTPException through, gunicorn "shop:create_app()" behind HTTPS.

Formulas

Guesses per second against a slow hashExam favourite
guesses/s = raw hashes per second / iterations
10 million SHA-256 per second, 1,000,000 PBKDF2 iterations: 10 guesses per second.
Lesson: The maths: hashing cost, commits and capacity
Number of passwords
N = (letters in the alphabet)length
8 lower case letters: 268 ≈ 2.09 × 1011.
Lesson: The maths: hashing cost, commits and capacity
Average time to guessExam favourite
time ≈ N / 2 / guesses per second
2.09 × 1011 / 2 / 10 per second ≈ 331 years.
Lesson: The maths: hashing cost, commits and capacity
Commits
many commits cost n × commit time, one transaction costs one
200 inserts with a 5 ms commit each: 1,000 ms. In one transaction: about 15 ms.
Lesson: The maths: hashing cost, commits and capacity
Salt collisions (birthday bound)
n ≈ 1.18 × √(number of salts) for a 50 % chance
32 bit salts: 1.18 × 65,536 ≈ 77,000 users. Werkzeug uses 16 random characters, far more.
Lesson: The maths: hashing cost, commits and capacity
Test suite time
time = tests × time per test
120 tests at 15 ms: 1.8 s, fast enough to run on every save.
Lesson: The maths: hashing cost, commits and capacity

595Big CountriesEasyWHERE with ORA country is big when its area is at least 3,000,000 or its population at least 25,000,000. One WHERE with OR does it.

Tips and traps

  • In the exam
    Inside a blueprint, link with the blueprint name: url_for("api.status") or url_for(".status") for the same blueprint. Use current_app instead of a global app variable, because with a factory there is no global app.Lesson: The application factory and blueprints
  • Remember
    login_required is a normal decorator (Advanced step 2). functools.wraps keeps the view name, which Flask needs, because the endpoint name comes from the function name.Lesson: Users, passwords and login_required
  • In the exam
    For bigger apps, Flask-Login manages the logged in user and "remember me", and Flask-WTF adds CSRF tokens to forms. They do the same jobs as the code here, with more cases covered.Lesson: Users, passwords and login_required
  • Remember
    With pytest the helper becomes a fixture in tests/conftest.py, and pytest passes it to every test that has a parameter called client: 
    import pytest
from notes import create_app

@pytest.fixture
def client():
    app = create_app({"TESTING": True})
    return app.test_client()
    Then run python3 -m pytest -q. A real run of exactly this printed "2 passed in 0.18s".Lesson: Testing a Flask app
  • Remember
    Flask turns an exception in a view into a 500 answer. An errorhandler(Exception) can log it and send a friendly message, but must pass HTTPExceptions such as 404 through unchanged, as the example does. Use app.logger, never print, so logs get levels and can go to files or a log service.Lesson: Configuration, errors and logging

Step 4Web and APIs · Django: the framework with everything built in

4.1

Django basics: project, URLs, views, templates, models and admin

Open chapter

Project and apps, urlpatterns, views, templates, models with QuerySets, and the admin site.

Key ideas

  • Project django-admin startproject mysite, python manage.py startapp books, add "books" to INSTALLED_APPS. manage.py runserver, makemigrations, migrate, createsuperuser, shell, check --deploy.
  • URLs and views urlpatterns = [path("books/<int:book_id>/", views.book_detail, name="book-detail")], include("books.urls"). A view takes request and returns HttpResponse or JsonResponse. Http404, redirect, reverse.
  • Templates render(request, "books/list.html", context). {{ value|filter }}, {% for %}{% empty %}{% endfor %}, {% if %}, {% url "name" arg %}, {% extends %} with {% block %}, {% csrf_token %} in POST forms. Values are escaped.
  • Models class Book(models.Model) with CharField, DecimalField, ForeignKey(on_delete=...). Book.objects.create / all / filter(year__gte=1900) / get / update / delete. related_name for the other side.
  • Admin @admin.register(Book) class BookAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin) with list_display, list_filter, search_fields. path("admin/", admin.site.urls). Only staff users can log in.

Formulas

URL matching
checks for a URL ≤ number of patterns
Django tries patterns from the top: with 40 patterns the worst case is 40 checks, still well under a millisecond.
Lesson: The maths: URL matching, pages, queries and hashing
Number of pagesExam favourite
pages = ⌈ n / per page ⌉
1,234 books at 50 a page: ⌈24.68⌉ = 25 pages.
Lesson: The maths: URL matching, pages, queries and hashing
OFFSET of a pageExam favourite
OFFSET = (page − 1) × per page
Page 3 at 50 a page: LIMIT 50 OFFSET 100.
Lesson: The maths: URL matching, pages, queries and hashing
The N + 1 problemExam favourite
queries = 1 + n
A list of 50 books that reads book.author in the template: 1 + 50 = 51 queries. select_related makes it 1.
Lesson: The maths: URL matching, pages, queries and hashing
Hashing cost
guesses/s = hashes per second / iterations
Django 6.1 uses PBKDF2 with 1,500,000 iterations: 109 hashes per second give about 667 guesses per second.
Lesson: The maths: URL matching, pages, queries and hashing
Workers needed (Little's law)
busy workers = requests per second × seconds per request
200 requests per second at 0.05 s each keep 10 workers busy.
Lesson: The maths: URL matching, pages, queries and hashing

257Binary Tree PathsEasyDepth first search that carries the path so farLike listing every URL of a project whose urls.py files include each other. Walk down the tree, add each value to the path, and save the path at every leaf.
228Summary RangesEasyWalk once and close a range when the next number is not one moreThe admin and paginators show ranges such as 1-3. Keep where the current range starts and close it when the numbers stop following each other.
599Minimum Index Sum of Two ListsEasyA dict from name to positionLike joining two lists of favourites in the ORM. Store the positions of the first list in a dict, then look up each name of the second list once.
1441Build an Array With Stack OperationsMediumWrite down the operations, like makemigrations doesmakemigrations writes a list of operations that turn the old state into the new one. Here: read the numbers 1, 2, 3 ... in order, Push each one, and Pop it again when it is not in target.
1003Check If Word Is Valid After SubstitutionsMediumA stack, the same way template tags must closeA Django template is only valid when every {% block %} has its {% endblock %} in the right order. Here "abc" plays that part: push letters and remove "abc" whenever it appears on top.
1487Making File Names UniqueMediumA dict with the next free number for each nameWhen two users upload photo.jpg, Django storage saves the second one under a new name. Keep the next number to try for each name, so no name is checked again and again.
1048Longest String ChainMediumSort by length, then dynamic programming on a dictLike a migration history where every migration adds one field. Sort the words by length and, for each word, try removing one letter to find the best chain that ends just before it.
1912Design Movie Rental SystemHardSorted lists play the part of ORDER BY with an indexThis is a small ORM: one table of copies, a query "cheapest 5 shops for a movie" and a report "cheapest 5 rented copies". Keep sorted lists of (price, shop) and (price, shop, movie) so each query only reads the first 5.
736Parse Lisp ExpressionHardA recursive parser with a stack of scopesLike the context of a Django template: {% with %} adds names that live only inside its block, and inner names hide outer ones. Parse the tokens recursively and pass a new dict of names into every let.
472Concatenated WordsHardWord break with a set and memoryLike checking that a URL slug such as "redbookshop" is made only of known words. For each word, test every cut point and remember which endings were already solved.
Lesson: LeetCode practice

Tips and traps

  • In the exam
    Django calls its pattern MTV: the Model holds the data, the Template shows it, and the View decides what to show. It is the same idea as MVC, only the names differ: the Django view does the job of an MVC controller.Lesson: What Django is and why it has so much built in
  • Remember
    A project is the whole website with its settings. An app is one feature, such as books, accounts or payments. A good app does one thing, so you could even reuse it in another project.Lesson: A project and its apps
  • In the exam
    The test client does not check CSRF tokens unless you ask it to, so the POST in the example works without one. In a real project CsrfViewMiddleware is on, and every POST form needs {% csrf_token %}. The animation above shows what happens without it.Lesson: URLs and views
  • Remember
    Every value is escaped, so the script tag in the note shows up as harmless text. Only mark text as safe (the safe filter or mark_safe) when you made it yourself, never for text a user typed.Lesson: Templates
  • In the exam
    In a project you never call schema_editor yourself. You change models.py, run makemigrations to write a migration file, and migrate to run it. Chapter 4.2 goes much deeper into the ORM and migrations.Lesson: Models: Python classes that become tables
  • Remember
    The admin is for trusted staff, not for customers. Use a long random password for the superuser, keep DEBUG off in production, and consider a less obvious address than /admin/.Lesson: The admin site
4.2

Django in depth: ORM, migrations, forms, users and tests

Open chapter

Q, F, aggregate, annotate, the N + 1 problem, migrations, forms, users and permissions, transactions and TestCase.

Key ideas

  • QuerySets Lazy until read. filter, exclude, order_by, get, first, exists, count. Lookups: __gte, __icontains, __in, author__name. Q(a) | Q(b), ~Q(c). F("col") inside filter and update.
  • Aggregation and speed aggregate(Avg("price")) gives a dict, annotate(n=Count("books")) adds n per row. select_related for ForeignKey, prefetch_related for ManyToMany. only, values_list, bulk_create, indexes.
  • Migrations makemigrations then migrate. Commit the files. New fields need a default or null=True. Data migrations use RunPython with apps.get_model. migrate app 0001 goes back. sqlmigrate shows the SQL.
  • Forms form = BookForm(request.POST), form.is_valid(), cleaned_data, form.save(). clean_<field> for one field, clean() with add_error for several. ModelForm with Meta.model and Meta.fields.
  • Users, transactions, tests create_user, check_password, authenticate, login_required, permission_required, Group. transaction.atomic() all or nothing. TestCase rolls back each test, setUpTestData, self.client, assertNumQueries.

Formulas

Queries in a loopExam favourite
N + 1 without help, 1 with select_related, 2 with prefetch_related
20 books: 21, 1 and 2 queries.
Lesson: The maths: query counts, indexes and transactions
Time of a pageExam favourite
time ≈ queries × round trip + work
21 queries at 1.5 ms: 31.5 ms. 1 query: 1.5 ms plus a bigger row.
Lesson: The maths: query counts, indexes and transactions
Search without an index
rows read = n
1,000,000 books: the database reads all of them.
Lesson: The maths: query counts, indexes and transactions
Search with a B-tree indexExam favourite
steps ≈ logb(n)
With about 100 keys per page: log100(1,000,000) = 3 page reads.
Lesson: The maths: query counts, indexes and transactions
Rows from a join table (many to many)
pairs = books × average tags
20 books with 2 tags each: 40 rows in book_tags.
Lesson: The maths: query counts, indexes and transactions
Weighted average (LeetCode 1251)
average = Σ(price × units) / Σunits
(5 × 100 + 20 × 15) / 115 = 800 / 115 ≈ 6.96.
Lesson: The maths: query counts, indexes and transactions

1683Invalid TweetsEasyannotate(Length(...)) then filterA computed column: annotate each tweet with the length of its text, then keep the ones longer than 15.
1378Replace Employee ID With The Unique IdentifierEasySubquery with OuterRef, a LEFT JOIN without a ForeignKeyThe two tables share an id but have no ForeignKey. A Subquery that looks up the unique id for each employee works like a LEFT JOIN, and gives None when there is no match.
1068Product Sales Analysis IEasyFollow a ForeignKey inside values()With a ForeignKey, product__product_name in values() makes Django write the JOIN for you.
1661Average Time of Process per MachineEasyConditional aggregation with Sum(Case(When(...)))Group by machine. Add the end times and subtract the start times with Case and When, then divide by the number of processes.
1280Students and ExaminationsEasyCount per group, then fill in the zerosEvery student must appear with every subject, even with 0 exams. Count the exams per (student, subject) with values() and annotate(), then loop over all pairs.
1251Average Selling PriceEasySubquery for the price on the sale date, then a weighted averageEach sale needs the price that was valid on its date. A Subquery with OuterRef and two date lookups finds it, then Sum(price times units) / Sum(units) gives the weighted average.
1211Queries Quality and PercentageEasyAvg of a computed value and Count with a filterGroup by query name. Avg(rating / position) gives the quality, and Count with filter=Q(rating__lt=3) counts the poor results.
607Sales PersonEasyexclude with a subquery of idsFind the sales people with an order for the company RED, as a QuerySet of ids, and exclude them. Django puts the inner query into one SQL statement with NOT IN.
1193Monthly Transactions IMediumGroup by a computed month, Count and Sum with filtersAnnotate each row with its month (the first 7 characters of the date), group by month and country, and use filter=Q(state="approved") inside Count and Sum.
1174Immediate Food Delivery IIMediumSubquery for the first order of each customerFind each customer's first order date with a Subquery that sorts by date and takes one row, keep only those first orders, then count how many were delivered on the day they were ordered.
Lesson: LeetCode practice

Tips and traps

  • Remember
    The QuerySet keeps the rows it read. Looping twice over the same QuerySet runs one query, but calling filter() again builds a new QuerySet and runs new SQL. Save a QuerySet in a variable when you need it twice.Lesson: QuerySets: filter, Q, F, aggregate and annotate
  • In the exam
    In tests, assertNumQueries(n) fails when a change adds queries, so an N + 1 problem cannot sneak back in. In development, django-debug-toolbar shows every query of a page.Lesson: Fast queries: the N + 1 problem
  • Remember
    SQLite cannot change most column types in place, so the SQL above makes a new table, copies the rows and renames it. PostgreSQL runs a short ALTER TABLE instead. Django picks the right way for each database.Lesson: Migrations: changing tables safely
  • In the exam
    The usual view: if request.method == "POST", bind and check the form, save and redirect when it is valid. Otherwise make an empty form. Either way render the template, which shows the errors. In the template put {% csrf_token %} inside the form tag.Lesson: Forms: checking what users send
  • Remember
    Start every new project with a custom user model (class User(AbstractUser): pass) and AUTH_USER_MODEL. Changing it later, when tables already point to auth.User, is a painful migration.Lesson: Users, logins and permissions
  • In the exam
    login_required sends a person who is not logged in to LOGIN_URL with ?next=, as the 302 above shows. permission_required with raise_exception=True gives 403 instead, which is right for a logged in user who simply may not do this.Lesson: Users, logins and permissions
  • In the exam
    Look at the query count: inside a test the atomic() of transfer becomes SAVEPOINT and RELEASE, because TestCase already opened a transaction around the test. Outside tests it is BEGIN and COMMIT.Lesson: Transactions and tests

Step 5Web and APIs · Building APIs: Django REST framework and FastAPI

5.1

Django REST framework: JSON APIs on top of Django

Open chapter

Serializers, ViewSets and routers, pagination and filters, authentication, permissions, throttles and API tests.

Key ideas

  • Serializers class BookSerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer) with Meta.model, Meta.fields. serializer.data, Serializer(data=...).is_valid(raise_exception=True), validated_data, save(). validate_<field>, validate, SerializerMethodField, read_only.
  • Views and routers @api_view(["GET", "POST"]) with Response(data, status=201). class BookViewSet(viewsets.ModelViewSet) with queryset and serializer_class. router.register("books", BookViewSet). @action. get_queryset, perform_create.
  • Security DEFAULT_AUTHENTICATION_CLASSES (Token, Session, JWT). permission_classes: IsAuthenticated, IsAuthenticatedOrReadOnly, has_object_permission. 401 no credentials, 403 not allowed. Throttles answer 429 with Retry-After.
  • Lists DEFAULT_PAGINATION_CLASS PageNumberPagination with PAGE_SIZE: count, next, previous, results. SearchFilter ?search=, OrderingFilter ?ordering=-year. Always order the queryset. CursorPagination for feeds.
  • Tests and design APITestCase, self.client.post(url, data, format="json"), force_authenticate, assertNumQueries. Nouns in URLs, right status codes, one error shape, versioning, idempotent retries.

Formulas

Number of pagesExam favourite
pages = ⌈ count / page size ⌉
5 books at 2 a page: ⌈2.5⌉ = 3 pages.
Lesson: The maths: pages, limits and payload size
Requests allowedExam favourite
rate = requests / window
3/minute: the 4th request in 60 s gets 429.
Lesson: The maths: pages, limits and payload size
Wait time in a sliding windowExam favourite
Retry-After = oldest + window − now
Requests at 0, 10 and 20 s, a 4th at 30 s: 0 + 60 − 30 = 30 s.
Lesson: The maths: pages, limits and payload size
Requests per day at a limit
per day = rate × windows per day
100/hour: 100 × 24 = 2,400 a day.
Lesson: The maths: pages, limits and payload size
Payload size
bytes ≈ rows × bytes per row
20 books of 120 bytes: 2,400 bytes. All 50,000: 6 MB.
Lesson: The maths: pages, limits and payload size
Requests to read everything
requests = ⌈ count / page size ⌉
50,000 rows at 100 a page: 500 requests.
Lesson: The maths: pages, limits and payload size

No.ProblemLevelPatternHint
1408String Matching in an ArrayEasyCheck each word against the others with inLike the SearchFilter of an API: a word is a match when it appears inside another word. Two loops and the in operator are enough for small lists.
1207Unique Number of OccurrencesEasyCounter, then compare the counts with a setA validation rule in a serializer often counts things. Count each value with Counter, then the counts are unique when a set of them has the same size.
1640Check Array Formation Through ConcatenationEasyA dict from first number to pieceLike joining pages of API results back into one list. Each piece starts with a different number, so a dict from first number to piece finds the next piece at once.
911Online ElectionMediumPrecompute the leader after each vote, then binary search the timeLike an API that answers "what was true at time t". Work out the leader after every vote once, then each question is a binary search on the times.
2080Range Frequency QueriesMediumPositions per value, then two binary searchesLike an API filter ?value=4&from=1&to=2. Keep the sorted positions of each value, then count the positions inside the range with bisect.
2707Extra Characters in a StringMediumDynamic programming from the end of the stringLike splitting a URL into known resource names. best[i] is the fewest extra letters from position i. Either skip the letter at i, or jump over a dictionary word that starts at i.
381Insert Delete GetRandom O(1) - Duplicates allowedHardA list plus a dict of index sets, swap with the last item to deleteLike a load balancer that picks a random server where some servers count twice. The list gives random choice in O(1), the dict of positions finds an item to remove, and swapping with the last item keeps removal O(1).
715Range ModuleHardA sorted list of disjoint intervalsLike a cache that remembers which ranges of ids it already fetched from an API. Keep the ranges sorted and merged, and use bisect to find the ones that touch a new range.
2276Count Integers in IntervalsHardMerge intervals as they arrive and keep a running totalLike counting how many ids a set of API keys may read. Keep disjoint intervals sorted by start, merge every new one with the ones it touches, and update the total on the way.
1622Fancy SequenceHardStore one lazy formula a × x + b for every valueLike update(price=F("price") * 2 + 1) for every row at once: never touch each value. Keep one global formula and store each new value "undone" with the modular inverse, so the formula applies to it correctly later.
Lesson: LeetCode practice

Tips and traps

  • Remember
    Response(data) is not JSON yet. The renderer turns it into JSON for programs and into the browsable HTML page for a person with a browser. That page lets you try the API by hand.Lesson: Serializers and API views
  • In the exam
    SearchFilter and OrderingFilter come with DRF. For filters such as ?year=1965&author=2, the django-filter add on reads them from a filterset_fields list. Always order the queryset, otherwise pages can show a row twice.Lesson: ViewSets, routers, filters and pages
  • Remember
    Never trust ids or owners from the request body. The example ignores "owner": "bob" in the body and sets the owner from the token in perform_create. Mark such fields read only in the serializer.Lesson: Authentication, permissions and throttling
5.2

FastAPI: fast, typed APIs with automatic docs

Open chapter

Pydantic models, typed parameters, response_model, Depends, async def and the event loop, docs and pytest.

Key ideas

  • Endpoints @app.get("/books/{book_id}") def get_book(book_id: int). Query parameters are plain parameters, Query(10, le=100) adds limits. A Pydantic model parameter is the body. response_model, status_code, HTTPException(404, "...").
  • Pydantic class BookIn(BaseModel) with Field(gt=0), Field(min_length=...), Literal, nested models, @field_validator, @model_validator. model_dump(), model_dump_json(), model_json_schema(). Bad input is a 422 with locations.
  • Dependencies Depends(get_db) and Annotated[T, Depends(f)]. yield for clean up. Header() for tokens, OAuth2PasswordBearer for logins. app.dependency_overrides in tests.
  • Async async def only with awaitable libraries (httpx.AsyncClient, asyncpg). Plain def for blocking code, which runs in a thread pool. Never time.sleep or requests.get in async def. BackgroundTasks, lifespan.
  • Run and test fastapi dev main.py, fastapi run or uvicorn main:app --workers 4. /openapi.json, /docs, /redoc. TestClient(app) with pytest fixtures and parametrize.

Formulas

Time with awaitExam favourite
total ≈ the longest single wait
10 requests that each wait 0.2 s: about 0.2 s.
Lesson: The maths: concurrency, workers and timeouts
Time with a blocked loopExam favourite
total ≈ n × wait
10 × 0.2 = 2.0 s.
Lesson: The maths: concurrency, workers and timeouts
Requests one process can hold (Little's law)Exam favourite
in flight = rate × time per request
500 requests a second at 0.2 s each: 100 in flight at once.
Lesson: The maths: concurrency, workers and timeouts
Thread pool limit
requests per second ≤ threads / time per request
40 threads at 0.2 s: at most 200 plain def requests a second per process.
Lesson: The maths: concurrency, workers and timeouts
Workers
workers ≈ 2 × CPU cores + 1 (a common start for sync servers)
4 cores: 9 workers. Async servers often use one worker per core.
Lesson: The maths: concurrency, workers and timeouts
Timeout budget
total ≤ sum of the calls in a row
Three calls of 0.3 s in a row: 0.9 s. In parallel with gather: about 0.3 s.
Lesson: The maths: concurrency, workers and timeouts

1122Relative Sort ArrayEasySort with a key: (position in the order, value)Like an API that lists fields in a fixed order and the rest A to Z after them. A dict gives each wanted value its position, and the sort key puts the others at the end.
1200Minimum Absolute DifferenceEasySort, then only neighbours matterAfter sorting, the closest pair is always next to each other, so one pass finds the smallest gap and the pairs that have it.
1287Element Appearing More Than 25% In Sorted ArrayEasyCompare with the item a quarter further onIn a sorted list a value that fills more than a quarter must still be there a quarter of the length later. One loop, no counting.
1013Partition Array Into Three Parts With Equal SumEasyWalk once and count parts that reach a thirdThe total must split into three equal parts. Add numbers from the left and count each time the running sum reaches one third, then start again.
1237Find Positive Integer Solution for a Given EquationMediumTwo pointers on a function you can only callYou can only call the hidden function f(x, y), like a remote API that you want to call as few times as possible. f grows with x and with y, so start at x = 1 and y = 1000 and move one of them each call.
2069Walking Robot Simulation IIMediumMoves wrap around the border, so use the remainderThe robot only walks around the edge of the grid. One full lap is a fixed number of steps, so a huge step count shrinks to steps % lap, like a cursor that wraps around.
1801Number of Orders in the BacklogMediumTwo heaps: highest buy and lowest sellAn order book API: a buy matches the cheapest sell, a sell matches the highest buy. A min heap of sells and a max heap of buys (negated prices) give the best match at once.
1032Stream of CharactersHardA trie of reversed words, checked from the newest letterLike a WebSocket that gets one letter at a time and must say at once if the latest letters end a banned word. Store the words backwards in a trie and walk it from the newest letter back.
2642Design Graph With Shortest Path CalculatorHardDijkstra with a heap on every queryLike a gateway that finds the cheapest chain of services. Keep the edges in a dict of lists, let addEdge append, and run Dijkstra with a heap for each shortestPath question.
2286Booking Concert Tickets in GroupsHardA segment tree with the max and the sum of free seats per rangeA booking API must answer "first row with k free seats together" and "book k scattered seats" fast. A segment tree keeps the most free seats in a row and the total free seats for every range of rows.

Tips and traps

  • Remember
    Pydantic converts when it is safe: "3" becomes 3, but "3.5" for an int is an error, and so is the 13th month. Every problem is listed with its location, such as address.zip_code, which is exactly what FastAPI sends back in a 422 answer.Lesson: Pydantic: data that checks itself
  • In the exam
    Run the real server with fastapi dev main.py while you develop (it reloads on every save) and fastapi run main.py or uvicorn main:app --workers 4 in production. Then open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs.Lesson: Your first API: parameters, bodies and errors
  • Remember
    For real logins FastAPI has OAuth2PasswordBearer, which reads "Authorization: Bearer ..." and also adds an Authorize button to /docs. The token is usually a JWT signed with a secret key (chapter 6.1).Lesson: Dependencies

Step 6Web and APIs · Securing APIs and the web revision exam

6.1

API security: passwords, JWT, OAuth 2.0, CORS and OWASP

Open chapter

Password hashing, JWTs by hand and with PyJWT, OAuth 2.0 scopes in FastAPI, CORS and CSRF, and the OWASP API Top 10.

Key ideas

  • Passwords hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac("sha256", pw, salt, 600_000) or Argon2id. Random salt per user, stored as algorithm$rounds$salt$hash. hmac.compare_digest. secrets.token_urlsafe(32), never random. Keys from os.environ, never in git.
  • JWT header.payload.signature in base64url, HS256 = HMAC-SHA256. Readable by anyone. jwt.encode(claims, key, algorithm="HS256"). jwt.decode(token, key, algorithms=["HS256"], audience=..., issuer=...). Claims sub, exp, iat, nbf, aud, iss, jti. Short access, rotated refresh, kid for keys.
  • FastAPI auth OAuth2PasswordBearer(tokenUrl="token", scopes=...), OAuth2PasswordRequestForm, Security(current_user, scopes=[...]). 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer, 403 for missing scope, 404 for another user's object.
  • Browser rules CORSMiddleware(allow_origins=[exact list], allow_credentials=True, allow_methods, allow_headers). Preflight OPTIONS. Never * with credentials. CSRF: SameSite cookies and CSRF tokens. Headers: HSTS, nosniff, Content-Security-Policy.
  • OWASP API Top 10 API1 object level checks, API2 authentication, API3 property level (mass assignment, extra="forbid"), API4 resource limits, API5 function level, API7 SSRF. ? placeholders against injection. Rate limits with 429 and Retry-After.

Formulas

Entropy of a random secretExam favourite
bits = length × log2(alphabet size)
12 random lower case letters: 12 × log2 26 ≈ 56.4 bits.
Lesson: The maths: guessing, entropy, hashing cost and rate limits
Guesses to try every valueExam favourite
guesses = 2bits
A 6 digit code: 106 = 1,000,000 values.
Lesson: The maths: guessing, entropy, hashing cost and rate limits
Time to crackExam favourite
time = guesses × cost per guess / machines
With PBKDF2 at 0.12 s, one million guesses take 120,000 s on one core.
Lesson: The maths: guessing, entropy, hashing cost and rate limits
Chance to guess with a rate limit
P = attempts / values
5 tries on a 6 digit code: 5 / 1,000,000 = 0.0005 %.
Lesson: The maths: guessing, entropy, hashing cost and rate limits
Token bucket
allowed in t seconds ≤ capacity + rate × t
Capacity 10, rate 2 per second: at most 10 + 2 × 60 = 130 requests in a minute.
Lesson: The maths: guessing, entropy, hashing cost and rate limits
Birthday bound for random ids
P(any repeat) ≈ n2 / 2bits + 1
1 billion random 128 bit ids: about 1018 / 2129, practically zero.
Lesson: The maths: guessing, entropy, hashing cost and rate limits

Table: no. · problem · level · pattern
No.ProblemLevelPatternHint
2325Decode the MessageEasyBuild a substitution table from first appearancesThis is a simple substitution cipher. The first time each letter appears in the key it stands for the next letter of the alphabet. A dict holds the table, and spaces stay as they are. Ciphers like this are easy to break, which is why real systems use keys and HMAC instead.
1844Replace All Digits with CharactersEasyShift a letter by a digitEvery digit says how far to move the letter before it, the same idea as a Caesar shift. chr(ord(letter) + digit) does the move.
1528Shuffle StringEasyPut each character at its target indexA transposition: indices[i] says where s[i] belongs. Fill a list of the right length, then join it.
1461Check If a String Contains All Binary Codes of Size KMediumA set of every window of length kThere are 2k codes of length k, the same count an attacker must try to guess a k bit token. Put every window of the string in a set and compare its size with 2k.
187Repeated DNA SequencesMediumTwo sets: seen once and seen againSlide a window of 10 letters and remember each one in a set. A window that is already there is a repeat, like a replayed request id that a server must refuse. The answer is sorted here so the tests can compare it.
1980Find Unique Binary StringMediumCantor diagonal: differ from string i at place iTake bit i of string i and flip it. The new string differs from every given string in at least one place, so it cannot be any of them. The same trick proves that some sets cannot be listed.
721Accounts MergeMediumUnion find over e-mail addressesTwo accounts are one person when they share an e-mail, like linking identities in a login system. Union find joins every e-mail with the first e-mail of its account, then each group becomes one sorted account. The list is sorted at the end so the tests can compare it.
420Strong Password CheckerHardCount runs, then spend deletions where they save a replacementA strong password has 6 to 20 characters, a lower case letter, an upper case letter and a digit, and never three equal characters in a row. Short passwords only need inserts. Long ones need deletes, and a delete in a run whose length is a multiple of 3 saves one replacement, so spend deletes on those runs first, then on runs with remainder 1 (two deletes) and then three at a time.
2156Find Substring With Given Hash ValueHardRolling hash, walking from the rightThe hash gives the first letter the power p0, so it is easy to add a letter on the LEFT: multiply by p and add the new value. Walk from the end of the string, drop the letter that falls out of the window, and remember the leftmost window that matches. Rolling hashes also power rsync and duplicate file checks.
1392Longest Happy PrefixHardThe KMP failure tableA happy prefix is also a suffix. The prefix function of KMP stores, for each position, the longest proper prefix that ends there, and its last value is the answer. It runs in O(n), with no hash collisions to worry about.
Lesson: LeetCode practice

Tips and traps

  • In the exam
    Keep secret keys out of the code: read them with os.environ["SECRET_KEY"], keep a local .env file in .gitignore, and use a vault (AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault) in production. A key that was ever pushed to git is burnt: rotate it, because deleting the commit does not remove copies.Lesson: Storing passwords and secrets
  • Remember
    In a browser, an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookie is the safest place for a token, because JavaScript (and so an XSS bug) cannot read it. localStorage is readable by any script on the page.Lesson: Real tokens with PyJWT: expiry, refresh and key rotation
6.2

Web revision exam: HTTP, Flask, Django, FastAPI and security

Open chapter

Four papers that run in the page, eight bugs, the web traps, a design answer and a mock quiz.

Key ideas

  • HTTP Status classes 2xx, 3xx, 4xx, 5xx. 201 with Location, 204, 301, 304, 400, 401, 403, 404, 405, 412, 422, 429. Idempotent: GET, PUT, DELETE. requests.get(url, timeout=5) and raise_for_status().
  • Flask @app.get("/books/<int:book_id>"), request.args.get("page", 1, type=int), request.get_json(), return dict, status, headers. g, session, Blueprint(url_prefix=...), url_for, errorhandler, test_client().
  • Django and DRF Lazy QuerySets, Q, F, annotate, select_related and prefetch_related, makemigrations and migrate, reverse and resolve, autoescape. Serializer.is_valid() then validated_data, ModelViewSet with a router.
  • FastAPI Type hints decide path, query and body. Pydantic gives 422 with locations. response_model, Depends with yield, async def only with await, TestClient and dependency_overrides.
  • Security Slow salted hashes, JWT with pinned algorithms and short exp, scopes give 403, owner checks give 404, CORS for browsers, ? placeholders, caps on page size, secrets in the environment.

6DecodeError, InvalidAudienceError, okPyJWT 2 refuses to decode without algorithms=. A token with aud needs audience= as well (6.1)
732 64 32 22SHA-256 gives 32 bytes, which is 64 hex digits. token_hex(16) gives 32 characters and token_urlsafe(16) gives 22 (6.1)
8True TrueThe same key and message always give the same HMAC. compare_digest only changes how long the comparison takes (6.1)
9[True, False, True, False, True]172.16.0.0/12 ends at 172.31.255.255, so 172.32.0.1 is public. ::1 is the IPv6 loopback (6.1)
10True FalseA hash is the same for the same input. Different salts give different results, which defeats precomputed tables (6.1)

Lesson: The traps in one table
Table: no. · problem · level · pattern
No.ProblemLevelPatternHint
1629Slowest KeyEasyOne pass over the gaps between timesLike finding the slowest request in an access log: each duration is the gap to the previous time. Keep the longest, and on a tie the larger letter.
1701Average Waiting TimeMediumSimulate one worker with a clockOne server handles requests in the order they arrive. The clock is the time the server becomes free. A request starts at max(clock, arrival), and its waiting time is the finish time minus the arrival.
210Course Schedule IIMediumTopological sort with in-degrees (Kahn)The same problem as running database migrations or loading apps in dependency order. Start with every item that depends on nothing, and each time one is done, lower the count of the items waiting for it. A cycle leaves items behind, so the answer is empty.
399Evaluate DivisionMediumA weighted graph and a searchLike a currency API that only knows some rates: a / b = 2 is an edge from a to b with weight 2 and from b to a with 0.5. A query multiplies the weights along any path, or gives -1.0 when there is none.
1942The Number of the Smallest Unoccupied ChairMediumTwo heaps: free chairs and busy chairs by leaving timeThis is exactly how a connection pool hands out the lowest free connection number. Go through arrivals in time order, first free every chair whose guest has left, then give the smallest free one.
1438Longest Continuous Subarray With Absolute Diff Less Than or Equal to LimitMediumSliding window with a max deque and a min dequeLike finding the longest stretch where response times stayed within a band. Two deques keep the window's maximum and minimum in O(1). When max minus min is too big, move the left edge.
752Open the LockMediumBreadth first search over 10,000 statesA 4 digit lock has only 104 codes, which is why short codes need attempt limits. BFS from 0000 turns one wheel up or down at each step and skips the dead ends, so the first time it reaches the target is the fewest turns.
2050Parallel Courses IIIHardLongest path in a DAG, in topological orderLike a deployment pipeline where jobs run in parallel once their needs are done: a job finishes at its own time plus the latest finish among the jobs it waits for. The answer is the latest finish of all.
1235Maximum Profit in Job SchedulingHardSort by end time, DP with binary searchLike choosing which paid batch jobs a single worker should run. Sort jobs by end time. The best profit up to a job is either the best without it, or its profit plus the best among jobs that end by its start, found with bisect.
630Course Schedule IIIHardGreedy by deadline with a max heap of durationsTake tasks in order of their deadline. When the total time passes a deadline, drop the longest task taken so far, because that frees the most time while keeping the count. A max heap (negative numbers in heapq) finds it.
